This technique enables AI models to respond to user queries by referencing a specified set of documents, thereby supplementing their pre-existing training data with domain-specific or updated information [2][3]. By dynamically retrieving relevant text before generating responses, RAG allows large language models to use information that is not available in their static training data [3].

Theoretically, it allows a quantum computer to factor large integers quickly, solving both the factoring problem and the discrete log problem [4].

This field enables the study of electron dynamics, atomic physics phenomena like photo-emission delay, and molecular processes such as charge-transfer [2].

Transmons are the default qubit used in most large-scale quantum processors, including Google's Willow processor [1]. This specific qubit is a special type of circuit designed with a shunted capacitor to mitigate noise and operates as a charge-phase hybrid based on the Cooper pair box model [2].

Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman received the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their discoveries concerning modified nucleosides that enabled the development of effective mRNA vaccines against COVID-19 [1][3]. Their work underlies the creation of the best-known mRNA vaccines produced by BioNTech/Pfizer and Moderna [3].

Transformers are a family of artificial neural network architectures based on the multi-head attention mechanism that process input data like text or images as sequences of tokens [2]. Developed in 2017, they became the model of choice for natural language processing and form the foundation for large models such as GPT and Gemini [3][4]. These models utilize parallel processing to improve training efficiency and allow the self-attention mechanism to determine the relative importance of each token within a sequence [4].
